fresh_repro_baseline_vs_candidate.note: Every case is built fresh under mktemp -d -p /var/tmp; the same probe scripts were run against both byte sets in the same session.

B2_control_byte_records: is_control_shaped() + refusal in both engines' evaluate_path before any record is produced (control-character-refusal)

path_field()/san()/sanitize_field() now escape TAB/NL/CR/backslash and hex-escape every remaining control byte, so an emitted record stays structurally parseable by position and is lossless (a literal backslash is escaped too, so `\t` is unambiguous)
quarantine run_verify() rejects any engine record whose TAB field count is not 5 (ambiguous-engine-record) instead of parsing shifted positions
quarantine flow_one() refuses a control-byte target before the engine is consulted
B2_list_schema: the whole --list file is parsed and validated into arrays BEFORE any flow_one call
strict 2-column schema: a missing receipt column, an empty path, an empty receipt, a third column, and any control byte in either column are structural usage errors (exit 2) with no mutation
NUL anywhere in the list remains a usage error (pre-existing case preserved)
B1_ledger_authority: quarantine captures the ledger generation (sha + presence + control-byte cleanliness) at stage 1, BEFORE the authorization is derived
stage 4 re-derives against that stage-1 pin; any replacement during the hold window is class=FAIL ledger-generation-changed, even when the replacement re-states the same source path
stage 4 also refuses when the ledger carries control bytes

vault-independence rule added to all three tools: a vault path inside a quarantine staging tree (*/.ufo-quarantine/*) is refused (vault-in-quarantine), because it is destroyed by the same stage-5 rm it authorizes
both engines refuse a ledger containing control bytes (obsidian=ledger-control-bytes / ledger-control-bytes)

cross_seat_note.engine_preference: cand-b2-quarantine.sh resolves its receipt engine as SOUJI_VERIFY_BIN > cand-b2-verify.sh > cand-merge-verify.sh > installed souji-verify.sh, so the composer's merged name is honored and an unpatched engine is only a last resort.

honest_limits: The two B1 variants here are deterministic substitutions. I did not reproduce an atomic in-flight race (the S07 four-second gate) against the candidate; the stage-1 pin closes the substitution class, and the S17 repair already covers the revocation variant, but arbitrary final-check-to-delete atomicity remains unproven.

Control-byte refusal is a fail-closed narrowing: a legitimate file whose name contains a TAB can no longer be quarantined by this tool. That is a deliberate trade (the tool's output format cannot represent it unambiguously) and it is recorded as a regression case, not hidden.
The G1 live-fleet guard case fails 2/91 in a shallow copied layout on BOTH the installed and the candidate tool; it is a layout artifact. All lane-layout runs are green.
The host /tmp DISK QUOTA is active: a bare `--selftest` without TMPDIR=/var/tmp fails with 'Disk quota exceeded' on unpatched tools too. This is a host issue, not a tool defect.
No live-fleet mutation, no commit, no LOG.md edit by this seat — per the lane rule that workers write only their assigned files.
